title: Pulse Beam — Spatial Rebrand + Component Design Law
page0: Rework and rebrand Pulse as Pulse Beam. Preserve everything that already exists and works, but establish an end-to-end premium spatial theme, elegant gesture navigation, a permanent monumental room for the live Funnel systems, and clear standards because many components need UI overhauls. The reference image is atmosphere evidence, not a prescribed solution. Ask the Funnel open-endedly what the best complete product architecture should be, then build and publish it.
correctedQuestion: What should Pulse Beam become—spatially, visually, behaviorally, and operationally—so its active tools and Funnel systems feel like permanent parts of everyday digital life, while every existing capability survives migration and every component can converge toward one elegant design law?
materialQuestions: What deserves to be a permanent place in Beam rather than an app, panel, tab, or drawer?
How should a user move between permanent places so navigation feels spatial and habitual rather than menu-driven?
Which qualities in the reference atmosphere matter independent of the pictured content?
What visual and material laws can make hundreds of unrelated components feel native to one environment without erasing their functional identity?
What information, controls, data, shortcuts, provenance, and state must never be lost during a component UI migration?
How should legacy components participate immediately before they receive bespoke redesigns?
What measurable criteria distinguish a truly Beam-native component from a merely recolored legacy component?
How should the active Funnel systems become a monument with real utility instead of decorative visualization?
What motion, audio, lighting, and material behavior communicate that the Funnel system is alive without becoming distracting?
How should mobile gesture navigation, desktop navigation, accessibility, touch targets, and reduced-motion preferences map to the same mental model?
How should new permanent Beam spaces be added later without another shell rewrite?
How should Pulse/Refinery measure migration progress and verify that no capability was lost?

answer.thesis: Replace Pulse's page-like shell with a spatial shell built from registered permanent Beam Spaces. Keep tools/components intact as capabilities. Wrap legacy UI with a compatibility design layer now, migrate components against a strict Beam Design Law over time, and make the Funnel Hall a permanent live space rather than a tool window.

productIdentity.law: Internal IDs, routes, storage keys and component identities remain backward-compatible unless explicitly version-migrated. Rebrand changes product presentation, spatial shell and design contract—not existing capability identity.

beamSpaces.registry: Declarative list of permanent top-level spaces. Adding a space must be data/config first, shell rewrite last.

initial.name: Create
initial.role: Everyday creation/workspace. Active runnable tools and component work appear here.

initial.name: Funnel Hall
initial.role: Permanent monumental room showing the live/current Funnel architecture, active/candidate law state, specialist Funnels, receipts/telemetry entry points and traceable relationships.
initial.navigation: one horizontal gesture from Create; explicit Hall control on desktop/keyboard

beamSpaces.futureRule: Library, Refinery, Worlds or other systems become permanent spaces only when their frequency/context justifies a place rather than an overlay/tool.

mobile: Horizontal swipe on unclaimed workspace changes Beam Space.
Gestures inside a tool, input, slider, canvas or scrollable component belong to that component and must not trigger global navigation.
A space transition requires distance + velocity threshold and provides reversible visual feedback.
gestureLaw.accessibility: Every gesture has a visible/clickable alternative; reduced-motion mode replaces travel animation with a short fade.

evidenceFromReference: objects feel suspended rather than boxed into a dashboard
subtle depth separation instead of loud gradients
quality comes from proportion, light falloff and empty space more than ornament
forbidden: visual noise used to imply complexity

designLaw.name: Beam Design Law v1
invariants: Function before chrome: visual migration may not remove existing controls, inputs, states or actions.
Primary view is sparse; complexity is revealed contextually.
Every interactive target is at least 44 CSS px on touch surfaces.
No horizontal overflow at supported mobile widths unless the component's core function explicitly requires it.
Typography, spacing, radius, materials, focus rings and state colors use Beam tokens.
White is primary emphasis; ice blue is information/selection; emerald means verified/live/success only.
Surfaces float through depth and material, not heavy boxes.
Controls use consistent hierarchy: primary, secondary, quiet, destructive.
State is visible without relying only on color.
Reduced motion, keyboard focus and readable contrast are first-class.

migration.law: No destructive redesign. Each component moves through compatibility → audited → native while retaining behavior/data/identity.

levels.requirements: Loads and functions inside Beam; compatibility layer applies tokens/touch/focus/scroll normalization.
levels.meaning: Usable now, not yet considered redesigned.

levels.requirements: Behavior inventory captured; controls/actions/states compared before/after; mobile overflow/touch/accessibility checks pass.
Component intentionally redesigned to Beam Design Law; behavior parity verified; provenance preserved; bespoke layout uses Beam interaction hierarchy.

funnelHall.role: Monument + live observatory + useful control room.
scene: reflective dark floor with restrained highlights
suspended central Funnel constellation rendered from current graph data
transparent glass cone/ring structures that move slowly
emerald active/verified law and live-state light
quiet spatial hum opt-in/low-volume, disabled by reduced-motion/sound preferences
utility: tap/select a Funnel to inspect purpose/state/dependencies
trace a path through the graph
return to Create with opposite gesture
funnelHall.principle: If live graph/state data is unavailable, show an explicit unavailable state rather than decorative fake activity.

compatibilityLayer.purpose: Make the existing component estate visually coherent immediately without pretending every component has been redesigned.
behavior: Inject Beam tokens and base controls into same-origin embedded tools.
Normalize typography, inputs, buttons, focus, panel depth, scrollbars and touch sizing.
Never rename, delete or conceal a component control solely for visual consistency.
Mark compatibility mode visibly in audit data, not in normal user chrome.

audit.name: Beam Readiness
audit.rule: A component becomes Beam-native only through explicit checks; global CSS does not count as a migration.

implementation.retireMeaning: Files remain in history/repo for provenance; live Pulse shell stops loading them.

acceptance: Ultra Funnel candidate issues valid BlueprintReceipt and ExecutionReceipt for this rebrand.
Pulse displays Pulse Beam branding while legacy internal IDs/routes remain intact.
Create and Funnel Hall are permanent registered Beam Spaces.
Mobile can move Create → Funnel Hall and back with horizontal gesture without stealing gestures from interactive component surfaces.
Every gesture has a visible alternative.
Funnel Hall renders actual current Funnel graph data rather than a static image.
Funnel Hall visually distinguishes v44 ACTIVE from Ultra CANDIDATE.
Existing components remain discoverable/openable and retain their existing IDs/data/routes.
Same-origin legacy components receive compatibility styling without hiding controls.
Beam Design Law is documented and available inside Pulse.
Beam Readiness audit distinguishes compatibility from true native migration.
No-loss parity data is generated for migrated components.
Reduced motion and audio-off preferences are respected.
